newsitem.title: USA: U.S. sees no significant diversion of food.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sees no significant diversion of food.

text.p: The United States is unaware of any significant diversion of food aid to North Korea's military, despite charges by a congressional delegation that has just visited Pyongyang, officials said on Thursday.

"As far as we are able to judge, nearly all our assistance thus far has been directed at helping young children, particularly children under six," State Department spokesman James Rubin told reporters.
Rubin added: "We have no indication that there has been any significant diversion of the assistance we have provided."

The United States, a major food donor to North Korea, has provided $52 million this year through the U.N. World Food Program to help stave off a famine caused by two years of disastrous floods compounded now by a drought.
A U.S. congressional delegation said after visiting the secretive Stalinist country that it saw evidence food aid may have wound up on the plates of North Korea's military.
Rubin said: "We believe the World Food Program, with experienced in-country staff, has been carefully monitoring the distribution of assistance (and aid) has gone to the right places."
